decision.reason: Coral reefs and kelp forests share reusable underwater structure that changes three-dimensional movement, line-of-sight, concealment, collision risk, route choice and refuge geometry. ARCH-SUBMERGED supplies underwater medium/depth behavior but not dense persistent vertical/horizontal structure, while ARCH-FOREST is terrestrial and should not be overloaded with marine semantics.

archetypes.name: Aquatic Structure / Dense Submerged Habitat
archetypes.baseline_scope: Submerged environments where persistent biological or mineral structure creates dense three-dimensional corridors, barriers, cover, vertical layers and refuge spaces within the water column.
reusable_behavior: three-dimensional route choice around dense structure
restricted sightlines and strong local concealment
collision and entanglement exposure where structure is fragile dense or mobile
vertical layering from bottom to upper water column
refuge pockets channels arches canopies and openings
structure-dependent current breaks and sheltered microareas
navigation landmarks formed by persistent underwater structure
excluded_or_deferred: exact water chemistry temperature salinity or nutrient state
storm surge tides or wave severity
evidence_basis: ENV-03 explicit reef/kelp structural behavior gap watch item
owner-approved ENV-07 Coral Reef and Kelp Forest expansion scope

non_promotions.reason: The existing Coastal Interface archetype already owns land-water boundary behavior; beach and exposed shore morphology can be preset parameterization with Open Country as needed.

Alternating exposed/submerged soft coastal ground is a compound coastal-wetland condition. Tidal timing and surge severity remain later hydrology/weather authority rather than a new structural archetype.

The defining expansion is depth, darkness, isolation and pressure parameterization in the submerged medium. Pressure and extreme darkness remain ENV-12/11-style condition authority rather than new topology.
Trench relief is preset-local topography inside a submerged environment. A new trench archetype would duplicate depth/topography semantics without enough reusable cross-preset behavior.
